meta.title_plain: The year Steffi Graf won everything in tennis
meta.teaser: In 1988, a 19-year-old won all four Grand Slams plus Olympic gold.

page.title: The year Steffi Graf won everything in tennis
page.sub: The story of Steffi Graf and her Golden Slam
page.bigIdea: In 1988, Steffi Graf won all four Grand Slams and Olympic gold in one year. Nobody else has ever done this Golden Slam in a single year.

cards.title: A racket in the living room
cards.front: Steffi's first tennis lessons didn't happen on a court. Where were they?
cards.back: At age 3, her dad taught her to swing a wooden racket in the family living room. She played on a real court at 4 and entered her first tournament at 5.
cards.tryit: Do 20 slow shadow swings at home, no ball. Focus only on a smooth, full swing.

cards.title: Losing first, climbing slowly
cards.front: Steffi played her first pro match at 13. Did she win?
cards.back: No. She lost 6–4, 6–0 to former No. 1 Tracy Austin. She won no titles for three years, but her ranking kept climbing: 98, then 22, then 6.
cards.tryit: Write down one tennis loss you had. Next to it, write one thing it taught you.

cards.title: Four hours a day
cards.front: How hard did young Steffi train?
cards.back: Up to four hours a day, sometimes straight from the airport. But her dad limited her tournaments so she wouldn't burn out. In 1985 she played 10 events; a rival played 21.
cards.tryit: Plan your tennis week: pick practice days and one rest day. Rest helps you improve too.

cards.title: The 34-minute final
cards.front: The 1988 French Open final was the shortest Grand Slam final ever. How short?
cards.back: Steffi won 6–0, 6–0 in just 34 minutes. Her opponent won only 13 points. Tennis fans call a 6–0, 6–0 win a 'double bagel'.
cards.tryit: Play a 10-point game. Try to win each point with your best shot, like Steffi's forehand.

cards.title: Comeback, then gold
cards.front: At Wimbledon, Steffi lost the first set to six-time champion Martina Navratilova. Then what?
cards.back: She won six games in a row and took the title. She then won the US Open and Olympic gold in Seoul. She was 19.
cards.tryit: Next time you lose a set, take three deep breaths and pick one thing to change.

quiz.q: How old was Steffi when her dad first taught her to swing a racket?
quiz.hint: She was younger than when she played her first tournament.
quiz.why: Her dad taught her to swing a wooden racket at home when she was 3.

quiz.q: What did Steffi's dad do so she wouldn't burn out?
opts: Limited how many tournaments she played
quiz.hint: Compare her 10 events in 1985 with her rival's 21.
quiz.why: He kept her schedule small so she stayed fresh while still training hard.

quiz.hint: Think about the word 'golden' and what you win at the Olympics.
quiz.why: A Golden Slam means winning all four Grand Slams and an Olympic gold medal.

quiz.q: How did Steffi do in her very first pro match, at 13?
opts: She lost to a former No. 1
quiz.hint: Card 2 is about losing first and climbing slowly.
quiz.why: She lost 6–4, 6–0 to Tracy Austin, then kept improving year by year.

page.think: Steffi lost a lot at first and won no titles for three years, but she kept climbing. What is one tennis skill you'd keep practising even if results came slowly?
